title: T-Count Study: 0 Gates
lesson: Start with a Clifford-only reference before adding T gates.
brief: This four-qubit mirror circuit is the reference case with no T gates. Protect it with up to two checks. You will compare it with versions that contain more T and T† gates. Empty columns mark the T sites used by the later versions.
learning_moment: This is the baseline for the T-count study. Under this puzzle's phase-flip-heavy noise, X checks can flag Z errors. With no T gates, those checks have more freedom to span the circuit. Record the best Fidelity you can reach while keeping at least 85% of runs, then compare it with the following versions. This result is the starting point for the series, not a universal benchmark for every circuit.
hint: Phase-flip errors are Z errors. Which Pauli anticommutes with Z? You have two checks; you may need both. Note Fidelity and Yield before moving on.
reflection: Across the series, what changed in legal check placements, Fidelity, and Yield? What else changed besides T count?
noise_note: Most modeled errors are phase flips (Z errors).

noise.label: dephasing-dominated (Z-biased) level noise, same for the whole series

explanation: Most errors here are phase flips. Each check starts as Z, but the first H turns it into X, so for most of the circuit both are X checks, which see phase flips.
One watches q0 and q1, the other q2 and q3, and both reach the middle CNOTs. The last H turns them back into Z, so both end at the readout.
With no T gates, nothing blocks an X check anywhere.
